summaries.summary: Language modeling provides context for NLP and ASR, while Transformers address LSTM sequential constraints using attention, parallelization, and SOTA language modeling results.
Recent standard transformer developments emphasize unsupervised pre-training and state-of-the-art NLP benchmarks, including BERT with a deep bidirectional transformer architecture.
Transformer-XL is another architecture of interest that introduces recurrence in a self-attention model.
Research has mostly focused on English, making performance on morphologically richer agglutinative Finnish interesting.
This project explores BERT and Transformer-XL for Finnish language modeling using BIBREF8 data, BERT probability approximation, and Transformer-XL sub-word units.
The work includes approximation of perplexity using a BERT architecture.
The work includes using Transformer-XL architecture with sub-word units.
The work compares Transformer and LSTM models as language models in comparable settings with an agglutinative language.
A language model assigns meaningful probabilities to token sequences by estimating the joint conditional probability P(X).
Perplexity (PPL) is an intrinsic Language Models evaluation defined using inverse token-set probability and the Tth root, where T is token count.
The approaches use BERT and Transformer-XL, with auto-regressive P(X) straightforward for unidirectional Transformer-XL but not bidirectional BERT.
BERT's bidirectional context complicates auto-regressive joint probability, so masking x_>i loses bidirectional advantage and an approximation is proposed.
Such approximations were explored with Bi-directional RNN LM's BIBREF9, and the authors define a pseudo-perplexity score for deep transformer models.
Original BERT uses Masked language modelling and next sentence prediction, while Finnish experiments use morfessor, boundary markers, and separate left-marked and left+right-marked models.
Next Sentence Prediction (NSP) is omitted from BERT pre-training, and input changes from SEGMENT-PAIR to SINGLE SEGMENT.
Transformer-XL uses recurrence, cached hidden states, relative positional embeddings, unidirectional perplexity calculation, and sub-word units for Finnish.
Finnish text data from BIBREF13 has around 144 million word tokens, 4.2 million unique tokens, Morfessor 2.0 with α of 0.001, 34K and 19K vocabularies, and 2850 YLE test articles.
All BERT experiments were trained for 500K steps in Python with Tensorflow on a single NVIDIA Tesla V100 32 GB graphic card.
Optimal BERT parameters used Adam, a maximum sequence length of 300 covering 98 percent of training data, and around 15 days training time.
Masked LM loss and accuracy concern masked-token prediction, with Finnish losses differing from English BERT trained on 3.3 Billion words versus 144 million words.
Pseudo-perplexity results on the test data-set show both BERT models confident, with lower left-marked values than left-right-marked.
BERT perplexity cannot be directly compared with unidirectional LSTM perplexity, but comparisons could use Bi-directional LSTM, downstreaming tasks, or masked-token prediction accuracy.
All Transformer-XL experiments were trained for 500K steps in Python with PyTorch on a single NVIDIA Tesla V100 32 GB graphic card.
Transformer-XL experiments compare longer Segment and Memory length against larger models, using Adam and a cosine annealing learning rate scheduler.
Left+right-marked Transformer-XL models train better, the left-right-marked large model(32-32) performs best, and Transformer-XL outperforms BIBREF19 by 27%.
Transformer-XL and BERT have low perplexity and pseudo-perplexity scores but cannot be directly compared, requiring a downstreaming task for fair comparison.
Transformer-XL justifies migration from LSTM models with strong perplexity, while BERT pseudo-perplexity is inequitable and future ASR downstreaming comparisons are planned.
